title: Agentic AI vs ML-based Autotuning: A Comparative Study for Loop Reordering Optimization
problem: Traditional ML-based autotuning approaches for HPC code optimization require expensive compile-run evaluations and lack adaptability for large applications. Emerging Agentic AI systems offer alternative optimization paradigms with unclear practical advantages.
motivation: HPC relies on code optimization to achieve performance on modern architectures. ML autotuning explores high-dimensional optimization spaces but suffers from expensive evaluations. Recent LLM advances enable Agentic AI approaches worth systematic comparison.
method: Comparative analysis between traditional ML autotuner and novel LoopGen-AI agent system using three LLMs (GPT-4.1, Claude 4.0, Gemini 2.5). Evaluation on loop-level optimization (loop reordering). Prompt engineering with Persona + Context Manager patterns. Analysis of convergence, sample efficiency, and decision quality.
key_novelty: First systematic comparison of Agentic AI (LLM-based agents) vs. traditional ML autotuning for HPC optimization, demonstrating Agentic AI's competitive performance with minimal program runs.
contributions: LoopGen-AI system using three different LLMs (GPT-4.1, Claude 4.0, Gemini 2.5)
Quantitative comparison: Agentic AI vs. ML autotuning for loop reordering
Evidence of effective Agentic AI performance with few runs (semantic understanding + dynamic feedback)
Analysis of prompt engineering impact (Persona + Context Manager patterns)
Demonstration that Agentic AI complements (not replaces) traditional ML methods

metrics.agentic_ai_convergence: few program runs to competitive performance
metrics.ml_autotuning_requirement: orders of magnitude more runs for peak performance
metrics.prompt_engineering_impact: significant effectiveness increase with Persona + Context Manager patterns

limitations: Evaluation limited to loop reordering optimization; applicability to other optimization problems unclear. Dataset and benchmark details not provided in abstract. Scalability to very large codebases not addressed. LLM model versions may become obsolete.
primary_theme: Agentic AI for HPC code optimization
